messages:
olivia: Quick check — planning a targeted activation for feature_x for Acme (org_id=12345) tomorrow 09:00 PT. Goal: verify enterprise contract gating + VIP behaviour. TL;DR plan below, please 👍 or call out risks.

rahul: LGTM overall. Couple Qs: how big is the activation slice? and do we need a temporary quota cap? :thinking_face:

olivia: Slice = org-scoped toggle (enable for exactly org_id=12345) + 5 internal seats for manual QA. Not percentage-based. We'll also set a soft qps cap of 30rps for that org during first hour.

elaine: confirm contract gating: flag should refuse enable unless `contract_tier=enterprise_premium` on account. I can add a precondition check in the feature gate.

matt: +1 to precondition. Also recommend `fallback_model=compact-v1` route if latency > 700ms or error rate > 3% for 5m. That avoids SLA impact for other customers.

tess: Ops ask — who is on-call during the window? I'll monitor dashboards if someone posts the runbook. @kim do you have capacity?

kim: I can be on-call for the first 90m. Share runbook link and I'll set alerts.

olivia: Runbook (short):
- Step 0: Preflight (30m before): run `deploy-bot preflight feature_x --org 12345` (checks below).
- Step 1: Set flag scoped to org: `redwoodctl flags set --flag feature_x --org 12345 --enable`
- Step 2: Enable QA seats: `redwoodctl flags add-seat --flag feature_x --org 12345 --user emails:"qa1@acme.com,qa2@acme.com,qa3@acme.com`
- Step 3: Monitor (first 60m): watch errors, latency, token costs, model fallback counts.
- Step 4: If anomaly -> run `redwoodctl flags unset --flag feature_x --org 12345` and notify customer success + eng.

deploy-bot: preflight OK — config schema validated, contract gating present, no conflicting toggles. Simulated traffic smoke passed (10k tokens/min burst). :white_check_mark:

rahul: Nice. A few nitpicks: add `max_concurrent_requests=20` per connection for that org for first hour. And add a telemetry tag `rollout=acme-2026-03-09` so we can filter.

elaine: I'll implement the precondition check now and push a small migration to ensure old orgs without `contract_tier` default to `standard` (do not allow).

matt: I added the fallback route config to the routing table. Also added a per-org rate limiter rule in staging.

olivia: Two contingency scenarios:
A) Partial degradation (latency spikes, model errors): switch route to `compact-v1` and keep flag on so we return degraded but functional responses to Acme.
B) Severe regression (error rate > 10% OR customer complaint): immediate rollback (unset flag) + postmortem.

tess: Monitoring dashboard links: https://console.redwood/mon/d/acme-feature_x (shared) — added countdown timer. Alerts: `acme_feature_x_errors` > 3% for 5m, `acme_feature_x_latency_p50` > 700ms for 5m.

kim: I'll pin the runbook in this thread and set PagerDuty escalation if alerts hit. Also will enable a temporary `silent-logs` mode for QA seats if they hit PII flows.

rahul: One more: is there an audit/logging requirement for contract gating? need to log who toggled and the `contract_tier` check result.

elaine: yes — audit record will include `actor`, `org_id`, `contract_tier`, `timestamp`, `flag_state`. I'll add that to the migration.

olivia: Perfect. Final asks before go: 
- @rahul add rate-limit config to the PR (small change)
- @elaine push precondition migration and mark ready
- @matt verify routing rule is deployed to prod infra
- @kim and @tess monitor during window

If no objections by EOD we'll go ahead. Thanks all :raised_hands:
